stories.headline: Pueblo Officer Fatally Shoots Man Who Allegedly Kidnapped Infant During Domestic Disturbance
stories.summary:
A Pueblo police officer shot and killed a man Saturday night after he allegedly kidnapped his infant during a domestic disturbance and refused repeated orders to stop reaching into a backpack. The incident began around 8 p.m. on the 400 block of West Ninth Street, where the man reportedly threatened the mother of his child with a handgun and threatened to shoot anyone who approached the residence. The woman and infant had an active restraining order against him.

The man fled the residence carrying the infant and stopped in a nearby parking lot, where he began reaching into a backpack. Officers ordered him to stop and to put the infant down; he placed the child in a stroller but continued reaching into the bag, at which point an officer fired. No weapons were reported found on the man, and the contents of the bag were not disclosed in police's initial statement.

The man was transported to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The infant was uninjured and the mother was treated and released with no serious injuries. The shooting is under investigation by the 10th Judicial District Critical Incident Response Team. The man's name was withheld pending family notification.

stories.headline: Cardinals Rally Past Rockies 10-8 as Hjerpe Shines in MLB Debut
stories.summary:
The St. Louis Cardinals defeated the Colorado Rockies 10-8 on Sunday at Coors Field, taking two of three games in the series. Cooper Hjerpe, a 25-year-old left-hander recalled from Triple-A Memphis before the game, threw four perfect innings in relief and struck out six in his major league debut to earn the win. Nolan Gorman's go-ahead, two-run home run capped a six-run fifth inning that proved the difference.

Mickey Moniak hit his 22nd home run of the season and drove in four runs for Colorado, while Jake McCarthy added a solo homer and three RBIs and TJ Rumfield went 3-for-the-day. Despite the offensive output, Colorado's bullpen faltered, with reliever Jimmy Herget absorbing the loss after surrendering Gorman's decisive blast.

The loss continues a difficult season for the Rockies, who next travel to New York to face the Yankees on Tuesday with Gabriel Hughes (0-6, 6.19 ERA) scheduled to start against Cam Schlittler (12-6, 2.04 ERA). St. Louis's Alec Burleson recorded his team-leading 103rd RBI of the season in the win.

stories.headline: Broncos Offensive Line Identified as Key to Breaking Pattern of Slow Starts Under Sean Payton
stories.summary:
With the Denver Broncos set to open the 2026 season against a brutal early schedule, head coach Sean Payton has acknowledged the team's persistent pattern of poor September play — going 4-7 in September games since taking over — and identified the offensive line as central to changing that trend. Four of the five starting linemen enter their fourth season together, with center Luke Wattenberg in his third year as the starter, giving the unit a continuity that new play-caller Davis Webb described as a significant competitive advantage.

The Broncos started 0-3 in 2023, lost their first two games in 2024, and went 1-2 before an 11-game winning streak last season. Payton's October record as Denver's coach stands at 10-3, reflecting a career-long trend in which he is 54-17 in October but only 31-30 in September overall as an NFL head coach.

Running the football effectively is seen as critical to easing pressure on quarterback Bo Nix and opening options for Webb's play-calling in his first season as offensive coordinator. The Broncos' rushing production collapsed after running back J.K. Dobbins was injured in Week 10 last year, and improving early-down efficiency has been a focal point of the offseason.

stories.headline: Analysis: Avalanche Traded Prospect Depth for Stanley Cup Window, and the Bill Is Coming Due
stories.summary:
A Sports Illustrated analysis published Sunday argues that the Colorado Avalanche have deliberately traded away future draft capital and prospects to sustain their championship contention window around stars Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, and Mikko Rantanen — and that the cost is now becoming apparent. The team made only 11 selections across the 2021, 2022, and 2023 drafts combined and holds no first-round pick until 2029, ranking 30th out of 32 NHL teams in prospect depth according to Daily Faceoff.

The Avalanche's top prospects heading into 2026-27 are defenseman Mikhail Gulyayev, forward Egor Shilov, goaltender Ilya Nabokov, defenseman Sean Behrens, and forward Beckett Hamilton. Behrens is considered close to NHL-ready and could see time with the big club this season, while Nabokov is projected to be approximately one year away.

The financial picture adds another layer of pressure: Colorado is projected to enter 2026-27 with roughly $404,000 in cap space, according to PuckPedia, leaving little room to add inexpensive complementary players. The analysis notes that a Stanley Cup banner hangs at Ball Arena as justification for the aggressive approach, but warns that rebuilding a depleted pipeline around expensive stars will be a slow and costly process.

stories.headline: Bicyclist Seriously Injured in Early-Morning Crash on North Broadway in Denver
stories.summary:
A bicyclist suffered serious injuries Friday after colliding with a motorist in the 300 block of North Broadway in Denver, according to the Denver Police Department. The crash occurred in the early morning hours and prompted an active investigation by police.

The incident is part of what authorities describe as a continuing pattern of severe bicycle collisions in the city. Denver Police issue Crash Alerts only when a collision results in serious injury or a road closure, underscoring the severity of this incident.

No additional details about the motorist or the bicyclist have been released. The investigation remains ongoing, and police are urging anyone with information to contact them.

stories.headline: Motorcyclist in Critical Condition After Crash on Chambers Road, Part of Denver's High Injury Network
stories.summary:
A motorcyclist was hospitalized in critical condition Friday after a collision with a motorist on the 4400 block of North Chambers Road in Denver, according to the Denver Police Department. The crash snarled traffic in the area, and the investigation into the cause remains ongoing.

The stretch of Chambers Road where the crash occurred falls within Denver's High Injury Network — the roughly 5% of city streets where approximately half of all traffic fatalities and serious injuries occur. The city has already designated $20.68 million for multimodal safety and operational improvements along that same corridor as part of its Vision Zero initiative.

Friday's crash adds to a documented pattern of serious motorcycle incidents across the Denver metro area this year. Statewide, motorcyclist deaths reached a record 165 in 2024 before declining slightly to 147 in 2025, with riders accounting for nearly 24% of all traffic fatalities despite representing just 3% of registered vehicles, according to the Colorado Department of Transportation.

stories.headline: 643-Mile Grassroots Gravel Race Draws Cyclists Across Colorado from Fort Collins to Trinidad
stories.summary:
The sixth annual North South Colorado bike race launched Aug. 28 from Fort Collins with 36 riders — out of nearly 70 who registered — setting out on a self-supported 643-mile route to Trinidad. Participants came primarily from across Colorado, with additional riders from California and Arizona, competing in a race that emphasizes self-reliance over spectacle and charges minimal entry fees.

North South Colorado exemplifies the rapid growth of grassroots gravel racing, a cycling discipline that has expanded significantly over the past decade and now attracts both amateur adventurers and elite competitors. Unlike corporately produced events such as Life Time's Leadville 100 series or the Unbound Gravel race in Kansas, North South deliberately maintains a low-key format that co-director Al Parks described in a brief pre-race meeting.

The race traverses some of Colorado's most remote terrain, and historically the majority of entrants do not finish: over the event's five previous runnings, only 78 riders have completed the full route. Organizers said the post office in Granby — based on prior experience — tends to serve as an unofficial overnight stop for many competitors on the first night.

stories.headline: Nob Hill Inn, Downtown Denver's Last Historic Dive Bar, Faces Closure by Sept. 30 Without Fundraising Help
stories.summary:
The Nob Hill Inn, widely recognized as downtown Denver's last remaining historic dive bar, is facing permanent closure by September 30 unless a community fundraising effort succeeds in time. The bar has become a landmark for longtime Denver residents seeking an alternative to the gentrified bar scene that has transformed much of the city center in recent years.

Details of the fundraising campaign and the specific financial circumstances threatening the bar's survival were not fully disclosed in initial reporting, but the September 30 deadline is firm. The closure would mark the end of an era for a venue that has served as a gathering place for Denver's working-class and artistic communities.

The situation echoes broader pressures facing independent bars and small businesses in downtown Denver amid rising rents, changing foot traffic patterns, and economic uncertainty. Community members have been urged to contribute to the effort before the deadline if they wish to preserve the institution.

stories.headline: RTD Reports Sharp Drop in Light Rail Theft as G-Line in Arvada Sees Most Recent Incidents
stories.summary:
Theft incidents on Regional Transportation District light rail lines have fallen sharply in 2026, with eight reported thefts through early September compared with 25 at the same point in 2025 — a decline of nearly 70 percent year over year. RTD attributed the most recent thefts to the G-line corridor in the Arvada area.

The G-line connects Denver Union Station to Wheat Ridge and Arvada and has historically been among the newer additions to RTD's light rail network. The agency did not specify the nature of the thefts or detail enforcement measures credited with the overall reduction.

The improvement in transit safety figures comes amid broader discussions about public safety on the RTD system, which has faced scrutiny in recent years over crime, fare enforcement, and ridership recovery following the pandemic. The downward trend in theft represents one positive data point for an agency navigating multiple operational challenges.

stories.headline: Denver Author Chris Vanjonack Releases Short Story Collection Shaped by a Decade of Relocation and Political Upheaval
stories.summary:
Denver writer Chris Vanjonack has published "Out of Body," a short story collection developed over a decade during which he moved across the country nearly every year, including stints in Fort Collins, Champaign, Southern California, and Columbus, Ohio. The collection, which Vanjonack discussed in an interview with the Colorado Sun, features characters imagining alternate versions of their lives against backdrops of political, ecological, and public health crises — without directly naming Trump or COVID-19.

Vanjonack, who teaches creative writing at Denver's Lighthouse Writers Workshop and is a recipient of the AWP Intro Journals Award, said the constant upheaval of his itinerant years made the collection possible rather than hindering it. His fiction and nonfiction have previously appeared in One Story, Electric Literature, and Barrelhouse.

The stories in "Out of Body" include a tale of a woman who finds a stranger appearing in every photo taken of her, a piece involving a clown encampment coded to invoke white nationalism and pandemic spread, and a decade-spanning narrative centering on a device that predicts the best day of its users' lives. Vanjonack describes the collection as being about dread and uncertainty, but also about possibility.

stories.headline: Colorado November Ballot Set as Secretary of State Releases Final List of Statewide Measures
stories.summary:
The Colorado Secretary of State's office has released the final — though still unofficial — list of statewide ballot measures voters will decide in November, according to Colorado Pols. The full scope of the ballot was described as extensive, though the complete list of measures was not itemized in initial reporting.

The November ballot is expected to include the income tax overhaul targeting top earners that has previously been reported, along with additional citizen-initiated and legislatively referred measures. Colorado voters regularly face among the longest ballots in the nation due to the state's robust direct democracy provisions.

The release of the final ballot measure list marks the beginning of the formal campaign season for ballot initiatives, with proponents and opponents expected to ramp up advertising and organizing efforts in the weeks ahead. Voters will have the option to cast ballots by mail, with ballots typically mailed in mid-October.

stories.headline: Republican Gubernatorial Candidate Victor Marx Hit with Record Fine; AG Candidate Michael Allen Linked to Controversy
stories.summary:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Victor Marx has been handed a record fine, according to a report by 9News anchor Kyle Clark, adding new turbulence to the GOP's 2026 statewide ticket. Colorado Pols reported the development alongside scrutiny of Republican attorney general candidate Michael Allen, whose nonprofit All Things Possible has been the subject of reporting that includes several Memoranda of Understanding drawing renewed attention.

The nature of the fine against Marx and the specific allegations involving Allen's nonprofit were not fully detailed in the initial Colorado Pols reporting, but both stories are generating attention as the November election approaches. Colorado Democrats were noted to be following the Florida-based reporting on Marx's nonprofit closely.

The dual controversies arrive at a critical juncture for Colorado Republicans, who are attempting to compete in statewide races in a state that has trended Democratic in recent election cycles. Both Marx and Allen are seeking offices currently held by Democrats.

topStory.headline: Iran Moves Toward Hormuz Agreement With Oman as Gulf States Reassess Security Posture After U.S.-Iran War
topStory.summary:
Iran announced Monday that negotiations with Oman over the future management of the Strait of Hormuz have reached their final stage, with a formal understanding expected to be registered with the International Maritime Organization within days. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the two countries, which sit on opposite sides of the strategic waterway, are close to an agreement establishing a temporary safe transit route through the strait. Both sides have previously raised the possibility of levying fees on commercial vessels transiting the passage, a prospect the United States has opposed.

The diplomatic developments came as Gulf states publicly grappled with the security lessons of the recent U.S.-Iran war. Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari, speaking at the Hili Forum in Abu Dhabi, said the conflict had demonstrated that Gulf nations cannot rely solely on their strategic partnership with the United States for protection. Qatar was among the countries repeatedly struck by Iranian missiles and drones in retaliation for American military operations during the height of the fighting. Al Ansari called self-reliance in security matters "the only way forward."

A senior Emirati official struck a more conciliatory tone toward Tehran while echoing concerns about Gulf unity. Anwar Gargash, a diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said Persian Gulf countries had failed to mount a coordinated collective defense during the conflict, with each nation largely acting independently. He described restoring a functional relationship with Iran as geographically unavoidable but cautioned that rebuilding genuine trust would be a far more difficult and separate task.

Meanwhile, Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun condemned ongoing Israeli airstrikes in the country's south, which local media reported killed 11 people on Monday. Speaking during a meeting with visiting French Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin, Aoun said the strikes undermined regional de-escalation efforts and called the killings of civilians unjustifiable crimes. The continued military activity in Lebanon adds another layer of instability to a region already unsettled by the aftermath of the U.S.-Iran conflict and rising energy prices driven by uncertainty over Hormuz transit.
